# One apt package per line, "#" starts a comment. scripts/system-packages reads
# this file and installs what it names, ahead of every language toolchain, in
# .github/actions/setup-toolchains. A repository without this file installs
# nothing, which is why it is adopted rather than shipped.
#
# What earns a line here: a dependency that links against a system library and
# resolves its headers through pkg-config. A Rust -sys crate, a Python wheel
# built from source, and a node-gyp module all do. The build passes on a
# developer machine that happens to have the library and fails in CI with a
# message about a build script rather than about a missing package, so the
# error almost never names what belongs here -- run `pkg-config --list-all` on
# a machine where the build works, or read the failing crate's build.rs, to
# find the name.
#
# Give the -dev package, not the runtime one: the build needs headers. And give
# the Debian/Ubuntu name, since these reach apt-get on a ubuntu-latest runner.
# A repository whose CI moves to a macOS or Windows runner has to solve this
# another way; this file is not read there.
#
# Two rules are enforced rather than assumed, and each fails the run naming the
# line: a line may hold exactly one package, and a package may not begin with
# "-". Both exist because the alternative is a guess passed to apt-get.
#
# Delete this paragraph and uncomment what you need. An adopted file holding
# only comments installs nothing and is not an error.
#
# libasound2-dev
# pkg-config
